title: Valuing a non-current asset
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:31Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Valuing a non-current asset
card: A non-current asset is something a business owns and expects to use for more than one year, such as a machine, a vehicle or a shop fitout.
It is recorded at its cost. Cost is the purchase price plus every other amount paid to get the asset ready for use.
These extra amounts include delivery, installation, testing and fees to set the asset up, such as legal fees when buying a building.
Costs of running the asset after it is ready, such as fuel, cleaning or a routine service, are not added to its cost.
draft.remember: Record an asset at its price plus all costs to get it ready to use.

a.q: Which of these is included in the recorded cost of a new oven bought by a bakery?
opts: The fee paid to have the oven installed
The flour used in the first baking batch
The electricity used each month by the oven
The cost of cleaning the oven each week
a.why: Installation is paid to get the oven ready for use, so it is added to the cost. Electricity and cleaning are running costs after the oven is ready, and flour is not a cost of the oven at all.
a.clue: Which cost is paid before the oven can be used?

b.q: Priya's Print Shop buys a printing press for $40,000 and pays $2,000 for delivery and $3,000 for installation. Six months later it pays $800 for a routine service. At what amount is the press recorded?
b.why: The press is recorded at $40,000 + $2,000 + $3,000 = $45,000, as delivery and installation get it ready for use. The $800 service is a cost of running the press after it is ready, so it is not added. That is why $45,800 is wrong.
b.clue: Add only the costs paid before the press could be used.

a.best: The fee paid to have the oven installed
